title: Kenyan Coconut Cassava
author: Chef Amina Hassan

relatedDish.note: KEN129 is a Coastal Cuisine category entry for Muhogo wa Nazi. The primary recipe with full heritage and cultural notes is KEN036 (Kenyan Cassava in Coconut Sauce). Both describe the same beloved coastal Swahili cassava preparation.

desc: Muhogo wa Nazi — cassava simmered in fragrant coconut milk with garlic, ginger, turmeric, and fresh coriander. One of the great simple pleasures of the Kenyan coast. See KEN036 for the full recipe and heritage.
longDesc: Muhogo wa Nazi is the coastal kitchen at its most generous — taking humble cassava and simmering it in coconut milk until each piece is infused with sweetness and fragrance. It is sold at coastal markets as a snack and served as a side dish with grilled fish throughout Mombasa and Lamu.
ingredients: 600g fresh cassava — peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Peel cassava, cut into chunks, remove woody central fibre.
Pre-boil in salted water for 20 minutes until almost tender. Drain.
Combine coconut milk, water, garlic, ginger, turmeric, salt, and sugar in a pot.
Bring to a gentle simmer — not a vigorous boil.
Cook for 10—15 minutes until cassava is completely tender and coconut sauce has slightly thickened.
chefTips: Pre-boiling cassava first gives better texture control.
A pinch of sugar balances the coconut milk beautifully.
commonMistakes: Adding raw cassava to coconut milk — it takes too long and the milk over-reduces.
cookingScience: See KEN036 for the full cooking science of muhogo wa nazi.
sustainabilityTips: Cassava is one of the most drought-resistant crops in Africa.
reheating: Gently on stovetop with splash of coconut milk.
culturalNote: Muhogo wa Nazi is a cornerstone of Swahili coastal snack culture — see KEN036 for the full story.
